title: Ferrari's First EV Sells for Record $40 Million
paragraphs: Ferrari's first fully electric car has been sold at auction for a record $40 million, making it the most expensive new car ever sold at auction.

The car, a specially customized Ferrari Luce, was sold by the auction house RM Sotheby's at a charity auction during Monterey Car Week in California in August 2026. Before the auction, it had been expected to sell for just over $1.1 million. Instead, it sold for more than 36 times that amount. The name of the buyer has not been revealed. All the money from the sale will go to the Ferrari Foundation to support its educational programs.

The car sold at the auction is known as "Chassis 0," because it is the first production chassis of the Luce program. It is a one-of-a-kind collector's model. It will return to Ferrari's headquarters in Maranello, Italy, before being delivered to its new owner in early 2027.

The previous record for a new car sold at auction was also held by Ferrari. In 2025, a specially made Ferrari Daytona SP3 sold for $26 million at the same event. However, the Luce did not break the record for the most expensive car ever sold at auction. That record belongs to a 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé, which sold for $142 million in 2022.

Ferrari unveiled the Luce in May 2026. It has a list price of €550,000. The car has four electric motors, one for each wheel, which together produce up to 1,050 horsepower. It can accelerate from zero to 100 kilometers per hour in just 2.5 seconds and has a top speed of 310 kilometers per hour. According to Ferrari, it can travel more than 530 kilometers on a single charge.
The car's design was created by LoveFrom, a creative company founded by Jony Ive, who previously designed many of Apple's most famous products, and Marc Newson.

However, the Luce's launch was not entirely smooth. Its design received strong criticism online, and Ferrari's share price fell sharply after it was unveiled. Nevertheless, the share price later recovered, helped by strong earnings and comments that orders for the Luce were in line with expectations.
